correctness.rationale: A line meets a smooth plane cubic in at most three distinct rational points. A cover with N/3 lines forces a partition of E(F_q) into zero-sum triples using rational flex O and chord-and-tangent law. The group sum is the unique nonidentity involution if one exists, ruling out equality exactly then. Cichacz’s zero-sum triple partition theorem provides the N/3 optimum otherwise. In the unique-involution case, a surjection G→Z/3 and the Goddyn–Halasz near transversal of H=ker χ yield N/3−1 disjoint collinear triples, then two rational lines cover the remaining three points, giving N/3+1. The explicit cyclic construction and small-field exact enumeration in the actual verify.py corroborate; the two published group existence theorems are essential infinite inputs, not checked merely by finite code. Finite fields of all characteristics allowed; rational flex and 3|N required.
